module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Cuban Primes

OEIS A002407 lists the primes that are differences of two consecutive positive cubes. The
sequence is conjectured to be infinite.

*References:*
- [OEIS A002407](https://oeis.org/A002407)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA2407

/-- A natural number is in A002407 when it is prime and is the difference of two consecutive
positive cubes. The addition equality avoids truncated subtraction in `ℕ`. -/
def A (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  p.Prime ∧ ∃ k > 0, p + k ^ 3 = (k + 1) ^ 3

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_7 : A 7 := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, 1, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_19 : A 19 := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, 2, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_37 : A 37 := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, 3, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_61 : A 61 := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, 4, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_127 : A 127 := by
  refine ⟨by norm_num, 6, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem not_a_91 : ¬ A 91 := by
  norm_num [A, Nat.prime_def_lt]

/--
This sequence is believed to be infinite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture : {p : ℕ | A p}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end OeisA2407

sources_consulted: OEIS A002407, complete entry read through the official OEIS data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A002/A002407.seq
review.notes: Checked all eight declarations. The definition and infinitude conjecture faithfully match A002407, whose entry states: “This sequence is believed to be infinite.” The research-open tag is consistent with that source. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, proved without sorry that A p is equivalent both to the stated prime cube-difference condition and to primality together with p = 1 + 3*k*(k+1). Verified the zero boundary, proved A p implies p ≥ 7, and confirmed that 91 is excluded despite being a consecutive-cube difference. Lean computations reproduce all 44 displayed OEIS terms; all six existing test proofs have no sorry dependencies. The direct OEIS webpage returned a browser challenge, but its complete entry was available from the official data mirror.
